title: Device-aware prefetch alignment and cross-plane communication coordinator for heterogeneous multi-GPU scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters (mixed memory limits, NVLink/PCIe topology), our current prefill/decode scheduling assumes uniform device characteristics. This causes microbatch skew, suboptimal kernel choices on devices with different L2/SM counts, and gaps where NCCL operations cannot be overlapped with compute effectively. The result is increased p95/p99 token latency during bursty workloads and higher unit cost from extra kernel launches and stalled comm windows.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight cross-plane communication coordinator plus device-aware prefetch alignment layer integrated into the runtime. Key pieces: (1) Device capability profiler collected at job start (SM count, memory bandwidth, NVLink topology, P2P latency), (2) per-layer kernel selector that biases choices by device capability and by expected sequence-length distribution, (3) prefetch alignment that staggers KV/prefill pacing across ranks to create contiguous NCCL-friendly windows, and (4) a cross-plane coordinator that negotiates short comm windows with the scheduling layer to intentionally batch small allreduce/allgather ops for overlap. The coordinator runs with soft priorities so it yields to latency-critical single-token decode when needed.

Why unique: Rather than only improving NCCL concurrency or token routing, this approach harmonizes three levers: kernel selection, prefetch pacing, and comm-window negotiation, and explicitly targets heterogeneous clusters (mixed GPUs and link topologies) where current strategies underperform.
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency reduced >= 12% on mixed-device 4x cluster compared to baseline
p99 decode latency reduced >= 8% on 8x heterogeneous cluster under synthetic burst load
No regression (>1%) in throughput for homogeneous clusters under steady-state traffic
New coordinator exposes trace spans and per-token cost breakdown in console; no significant memory overhead (+<2% GPU memory usage)
Automated test coverage: unit tests for planner heuristics and e2e harness reproducing microbatch skew scenario
design_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Profiling: lightweight on-job startup profiler (10-30ms) preferred to continuous heavy telemetry to avoid startup delays. We will cache profile results per image/runtime for repeated jobs.
- Kernel selector: maintain table of kernel candidates per op with device suitability scores (bandwidth-bound vs compute-bound). Prefer coarse-grained heuristic rather than expensive per-op autotune.
- Prefetch alignment: instead of forcing synchronous barriers, use micro-schedule offsets (0..N microticks) to shift when ranks prefetch KV and emit rendezvous. This creates NCCL-friendly aggregation windows while preserving decode latency for the rank generating tokens.
- Coordinator scope: keep state minimal (per-step window start/target duration) and implement as a local library in the runtime; avoid introducing a central controller to keep failure surface small.
- Safety/fallbacks: detect when overlap harms latency (via short windows or low util) and fall back to current aggressive-perf strategy.

Open questions: how to encode topology (NVLink chains) compactly; acceptable default offsets for families of devices; policy for mixed dedicated/private deployments with constrained networking.
implementation_notes:
Planned implementation tasks: 
1) Capability profiler (C++ runtime) + small protobuf metadata written to job metadata.
2) Kernel suitability table and scoring function integrated into kernel selection path.
3) Microtick scheduler: add microtick offsets to prefill pipeline and KV cache prefetch calls.
4) Cross-plane coordinator API: request_window(start_offset, duration_hint) + callbacks for granted/denied. Implemented in runtime scheduling layer, executed per-step.
5) Telemetry hooks: add spans in tracing for window negotiation and NCCL op aggregation.
6) Integration tests and stress harness (Pytest + harness that can simulate heterogeneous delay injection).

Engineering notes: prioritize minimal changes to existing prefill/decode hot paths; ensure compile-time flags to enable/disable. Prototype in feature branch runtime/mgpu-prefetch-alignment.
test_plan:
Unit tests: kernel scoring function, profiler parser, microtick arithmetic.
Integration tests: e2e with 4-node heterogeneous cluster in CI lab (A100 + A10 + V100 mix) with synthetic prompt lengths (prefill heavy vs decode heavy).
Stress tests: synthetic burst workload (spike of concurrent small decode requests) to evaluate NCCL overlap benefits.
Performance baselines: run benchmark suite (throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency) with and without coordinator; capture traces for correlation.
Monitoring: add SLO checks to console for p95/p99 rolling across deployments; add regression gate for runtime-1.21 release branch.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): runtime feature flag enabled on 1 cluster of dedicated capacity. Collect metrics for 72h.
Phase 2 (expanded canary): enable for internal QA jobs and 5% of hosted traffic with telemetry.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback if p99 worsens >5% for 30m.
During rollout keep fallback to legacy scheduler; include runtime toggles for force-disable per-customer.
metrics: p50, p95, p99 token latency (prefill and decode separately)
per-token GPU compute time and comm time (ms)
NCCL allreduce aggregation rate and average comm window duration
